sla_notes_intro: Standard French phonetics and phonology govern how sounds, syllables, stress and intonation combine in connected speech. Advanced learners must link and elide words correctly so that speech flows naturally.
sla_notes_details: Phonemes are the distinctive sounds (vowels such as [y] in tu and [ø] in peu, nasal vowels [ã] [ɛ̃] [ɔ̃], and consonants such as [ʁ]); words are divided into syllables that usually end in a vowel sound. French stress falls on the last syllable of a rhythmic group, and intonation rises for yes-or-no questions and falls for statements. Liaison is the pronunciation of a normally silent final consonant before a vowel or mute h: les amis [lezami], un grand homme [ɡʁɑ̃tɔm]; it is compulsory after determiners and pronouns, forbidden after et and before a h aspiré. Elision drops the final vowel of a short word before a vowel: l'école, j'aime, qu'il, s'il. Enchaînement links a final pronounced consonant to the next vowel: elle arrive [ɛlaʁiv]. Tongue twisters (virelangues) train articulation.
sla_notes_illustrations: Say the sentence Les enfants ont appris une histoire: liaison in les enfants [lezɑ̃fɑ̃] and ont appris [ɔ̃tapʁi], elision in une histoire without any change. Practise the virelangue: Les chaussettes de l'archiduchesse sont-elles sèches, archi-sèches.
sla_notes_daily_life: Clear articulation helps a learner understand and be understood in interviews, at French-speaking conferences and when listening to Radio France Internationale.
sla_exercise: What is liaison? Give an example.::Pronouncing a silent final consonant before a word beginning with a vowel, for example les amis [lezami].||Write the elided form of je + aime and le + école.::j'aime and l'école.||Where does the stress usually fall in a French rhythmic group?::On the last syllable of the group.

sla_notes_intro: Register is the level of language chosen according to the speaker, listener and situation. French has three main registers: familiar (familier), standard (courant) and formal (soutenu).
sla_notes_details: The familiar register is used with friends and family, with contractions and slang: T'as vu ça ? Il est bien, ce mec. The standard register is neutral and used at school and in the workplace: Avez-vous vu cela ? Il est sympathique. The formal register is used in writing, speeches and official settings, with inversion and the subjunctive: Auriez-vous l'obligeance de me le dire ? Learners choose between tu and vous, vocabulary such as bagnole, voiture and véhicule, and the negation with or without ne. Politeness formulas, tone and gestures also vary. Learners practise role plays that require changing register.
sla_notes_illustrations: The same request in three registers: Passe-moi le sel (familiar), Pouvez-vous me passer le sel, s'il vous plaît ? (standard), Auriez-vous l'amabilité de me faire passer le sel ? (formal).
sla_notes_daily_life: A student speaks differently to a classmate than to a headteacher or a consulate official, and choosing the correct register avoids offence.
sla_exercise: Name the three registers of French.::Familiar, standard and formal (familier, courant, soutenu).||Give a standard equivalent of the familiar word bagnole.::Voiture (car).||Which pronoun is used to address an official politely?::Vous.

sla_notes_intro: A complex text has several paragraphs and ideas linked together in a logical order. Coherence and cohesion make the text easy to follow.
sla_notes_details: Learners plan the text (introduction, development and conclusion), choose a topic sentence for each paragraph and support it with arguments and examples. Cohesion is achieved with connectors: addition (de plus, en outre), opposition (mais, cependant, pourtant), cause (car, parce que, puisque), consequence (donc, par conséquent, c'est pourquoi), concession (bien que + subjunctive), sequence (d'abord, ensuite, enfin). Pronouns and synonyms avoid repetition, and verb tenses are used consistently. The writing process includes drafting, checking grammar, spelling and punctuation, and revising.
sla_notes_illustrations: Sentence: Bien que la ville offre plus d'emplois, la vie y est chère; c'est pourquoi beaucoup de jeunes préfèrent rester au village. It uses concession and consequence connectors.
sla_notes_daily_life: Clear written texts are needed for application letters, reports and essays in examinations.
sla_exercise: Name two connectors of cause in French.::Car and parce que (or puisque).||What mood follows bien que?::The subjunctive.||What are the three main parts of a composed text?::Introduction, development and conclusion.

sla_notes_intro: Learners can work out the meaning of unfamiliar words by using clues in complex oral and written texts instead of looking up every word.
sla_notes_details: Strategies: read the whole sentence and the surrounding sentences for context clues; identify the word class (noun, verb, adjective); analyse word formation, that is prefixes (in-, dé-, re-, mal-), roots and suffixes (-tion, -ment, -eur, -able); use cognates (words similar in English or Swahili, such as importance, administration) while watching false friends (actuellement means currently, not actually); and use definitions and examples inside the text. Learners note new words in a personal lexicon with the sentence in which they appeared.
sla_notes_illustrations: In the sentence Le professeur a été très généreux, il a offert des livres à tous ses élèves, the learner deduces that généreux means willing to give.
sla_notes_daily_life: This skill helps a learner to follow news bulletins, notices and letters in French without a dictionary.
sla_exercise: What does the prefix dé- often express in French?::Reversal or removal (as in défaire).||What is a false friend? Give an example.::A word that looks like an English word but has a different meaning, for example actuellement (currently).||Name one strategy for guessing the meaning of a new word.::Using the context of the sentence (or word parts and cognates).

sla_notes_intro: Reference works help learners to find the meaning, spelling, pronunciation and use of words and to gather knowledge about topics.
sla_notes_details: A monolingual dictionary (Le Petit Robert, Larousse) gives definitions, grammatical category, gender, examples and pronunciation; a bilingual dictionary gives equivalents in Swahili or English. Abbreviations such as n.m. (nom masculin), v.t. (verbe transitif) and adj. are read carefully. A thesaurus lists synonyms and antonyms, helping to avoid repetition, and an encyclopedia provides in-depth information about people, places and concepts. Online tools include Larousse.fr, Reverso and Wikipédia en français; the reliability of sources is checked. Learners look up a word, choose the right meaning for the context and record it.
sla_notes_illustrations: Looking up the verb tenir in a dictionary shows several meanings (to hold, to keep, to run) and constructions such as tenir à (to be attached to); the learner chooses the one that fits the sentence.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translators, journalists and students use these tools daily to write correctly and to research topics.
sla_exercise: What does n.f. mean in a French dictionary?::Nom féminin (feminine noun).||What is the use of a thesaurus?::To find synonyms and antonyms of a word.||Give one online French reference source.::Larousse.fr (or Wikipédia en français).

sla_notes_intro: Advanced writing requires a wide vocabulary and control of complex grammar. This activity uses them to compose texts on a range of topics.
sla_notes_details: Grammar covers all tenses and moods: present, passé composé, imparfait, plus-que-parfait, futur, conditionnel and subjonctif; agreement of the past participle with preceding direct objects; relative pronouns (qui, que, dont, où, lequel); pronouns y and en; the passive voice and reported speech with sequence of tenses; conditional sentences with si (si + imparfait gives conditionnel). Vocabulary is enriched through word families, thematic fields (environment, health, technology, education, politics) and idiomatic expressions. Learners write descriptions, letters, articles and arguments on varied subjects, revise them and correct errors.
sla_notes_illustrations: Sentence: Si les gouvernements investissaient davantage dans l'éducation, les jeunes trouveraient plus facilement du travail. It uses si + imparfait and the conditionnel.
sla_notes_daily_life: This competence is used to write formal letters, reports and scholarship applications.
sla_exercise: Complete: Si j'avais le temps, je (venir) te voir.::viendrais.||Which relative pronoun replaces a phrase introduced by de, as in le livre dont je parle?::Dont.||Give the past participle agreement in: Les lettres que j'ai (écrire).::écrites.

sla_notes_intro: Listening comprehension in formal contexts means understanding lectures, news bulletins, speeches and announcements delivered at natural speed.
sla_notes_details: Before listening learners predict content from the title and key words; during listening they identify the main idea, the details, the speaker's attitude and the structure, taking notes with abbreviations and symbols; after listening they summarise, answer questions and give an opinion. Authentic materials are RFI and TV5Monde news, conferences and interviews. Difficulties such as speed, liaison, unknown words and accents are overcome by repeated listening and by focusing on keywords and connectors.
sla_notes_illustrations: After listening to a two-minute news item about climate change, the learner writes the note: cause - émissions de CO2; conséquences - sécheresse, inondations; solutions - énergies renouvelables.
sla_notes_daily_life: The skill helps a learner follow lectures and radio programmes and take part in international meetings.
sla_exercise: Name two stages of a listening lesson.::Before listening (prediction) and after listening (summary or answering questions).||Why is note-taking with abbreviations useful?::It allows the listener to record key information quickly.||Give one authentic French audio source.::RFI (Radio France Internationale) or TV5Monde.

sla_name: Responding to oral messages with confidence
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’écouter et de répondre à des messages oraux avec plus de confiance et autonomie.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels varés
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Oral interaction requires the ability to understand messages, ask for clarification and give comments confidently and independently.
sla_notes_details: Useful expressions for clarification are: Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ? Que voulez-vous dire par là ? Excusez-moi, je n'ai pas bien compris. To confirm understanding: Si je comprends bien, vous dites que... Comments and opinions use À mon avis, Je pense que, Je suis d'accord ou Je ne suis pas d'accord avec vous parce que. Learners use conversation strategies such as paraphrasing, hesitation fillers (euh, alors, eh bien) and appropriate body language. Role plays and dialogues practise responding to announcements, requests and invitations.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue: A - La réunion aura lieu vendredi à 10 h. B - Pardon, vous pouvez répéter l'heure ? A - À 10 h. B - Merci, je serai là.
sla_notes_daily_life: This helps in job interviews, telephone calls and travel situations, where clarification avoids misunderstandings.
sla_exercise: How do you ask a speaker to repeat something politely?::Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?||Give an expression used to give an opinion.::À mon avis... (or Je pense que...).||Why is paraphrasing a useful strategy?::It helps to check understanding and to express an idea when the exact word is unknown.

sla_notes_intro: Written French differs from spoken French in structure, vocabulary and register. Learners read different text types to identify these features.
sla_notes_details: Text types include narrative, descriptive, argumentative, informative, instructional and dialogic texts, and press articles, letters and advertisements. Features: complete sentences and punctuation, logical connectors, precise vocabulary, use of literary tenses in some texts (passé simple), layout (title, paragraphs, headings) and typical formulas (letter openings and endings). Reading strategies are skimming for the general idea, scanning for particular details, inferring, and summarising. Learners compare a spoken passage and a written one on the same topic to see differences such as omission of ne and hesitation words in speech.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a newspaper article the learner finds the title, chapeau, paragraphs and the passive and nominal forms used in headlines, such as Le président arrive demain.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading in French prepares learners for exams, official documents and higher studies in French-speaking universities.
sla_exercise: What is skimming?::Reading quickly to get the general idea of a text.||Name two text types.::Narrative and argumentative (or descriptive, informative).||Give one feature of written language that is not normally found in speech.::Complex sentences with logical connectors (or the passé simple).

sla_notes_intro: A theme is the central idea or subject developed in a text. Learners identify and explain the main themes in a variety of complex texts.
sla_notes_details: Steps: read the text carefully, identify the topic and key words, find the main idea of each paragraph, state the central message and support it with evidence from the text. Themes may include education, environment, migration, poverty, gender, technology or culture. Explanation can be oral or written and uses phrases such as Le thème principal est..., L'auteur cherche à montrer que..., Ce texte traite de... Summaries are written in learners' own words in about a third of the original length.
sla_notes_illustrations: For a text about deforestation the learner writes: Le thème principal est la destruction des forêts. L'auteur montre que l'agriculture et la production du charbon en sont les causes.
sla_notes_daily_life: The ability to summarise the main message is useful for study, work reports and discussions of news.
sla_exercise: Give a phrase used to introduce the main theme.::Le thème principal est... (or Ce texte traite de...).||What is the difference between a theme and a detail?::A theme is the central idea, while details support the idea.||How long should a summary be compared with the original text?::About one third of the original length.

sla_notes_intro: A debate is a structured discussion in which participants defend different positions on an issue. It develops speaking, listening and argumentation skills.
sla_notes_details: Preparation: choose a motion, research arguments for and against and prepare examples. Roles are the moderator, speakers for and against, and the audience. Useful language: Je suis pour/contre..., Selon moi..., D'une part... d'autre part..., Certes... mais..., Je ne partage pas votre avis parce que..., En conclusion... Rules include taking turns, respecting others, and supporting the position with evidence. Learners state their position clearly, respond to counter-arguments and conclude.
sla_notes_illustrations: Motion: Les téléphones portables devraient être interdits à l'école. A speaker says: Je suis contre cette interdiction car le téléphone permet de faire des recherches; certes, il peut distraire, mais des règles suffisent.
sla_notes_daily_life: Debating prepares learners for meetings, public speaking and participation in civic life.
sla_exercise: Give an expression to show disagreement politely.::Je ne partage pas votre avis (or Je ne suis pas d'accord).||Who leads the discussion in a formal debate?::The moderator.||How should a position be supported in a debate?::With arguments and examples or evidence.

sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A biography tells the story of a person's life. Learners research and write biographies in correct French.
sla_notes_details: Structure: title, introduction with name, dates and place of birth, family and education, main achievements in chronological order, difficulties, contribution and legacy, and a conclusion with an appreciation. Verb tenses: passé composé and imparfait in conversation-style texts, or passé simple and imparfait in formal biographies. Time markers include en 1961, à l'âge de dix ans, plus tard, ensuite, pendant que. Sources are books, interviews and the Internet, and must be acknowledged. Learners may write about a national figure such as Julius Nyerere or a Francophone figure such as Léopold Sédar Senghor.
sla_notes_illustrations: Julius Kambarage Nyerere est né en 1922 à Butiama. Après ses études à Makerere et à Édimbourg, il est devenu enseignant, puis il a dirigé le pays vers l'indépendance en 1961.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing biographies improves research and organisation skills and helps learners appreciate role models.
sla_exercise: Which tenses are common in a biography?::Passé composé (or passé simple) and imparfait.||Name two elements of the introduction of a biography.::Name and date and place of birth.||Translate: He was born in 1950.::Il est né en 1950.

sla_notes_intro: Translation is the transfer of the meaning of a text from a source language to a target language. Learners translate between French and Swahili using their own knowledge and reference books.
sla_notes_details: Stages: read the whole text, identify its type and purpose, translate meaning rather than word for word, choose suitable vocabulary and register, respect grammar of the target language, then check and revise. Difficulties include idioms (il pleut des cordes has a different equivalent in Swahili), false friends, gender and tense differences, and cultural terms. Techniques are borrowing, calque, equivalence, adaptation and modulation. Bilingual dictionaries and glossaries are used, and the final text is proofread.
sla_notes_illustrations: French: Les élèves doivent respecter le règlement de l'école. Swahili: Wanafunzi wanapaswa kuheshimu kanuni za shule.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translators work in government, media, tourism and international organisations such as the African Union and the East African Community.
sla_exercise: Why should translation be of meaning rather than word for word?::Because languages have different structures and idioms.||Translate into French: Habari za asubuhi.::Bonjour (or Comment allez-vous ce matin ?).||Name one translation technique.::Equivalence (or borrowing, calque, adaptation, modulation).

sla_teaching_aids: Logiciels variés de TAO|Dictionnaires bilingues en fonction de textes à traduire|Textes écrits authentiques ou fabriqués
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Computer Assisted Translation (CAT) tools help translators work faster and more consistently using translation memories, glossaries and machine translation suggestions.
sla_notes_details: Common tools include OmegaT (free), Trados, MemoQ and online editors such as Google Translator Toolkit successors, and DeepL or Google Translate for machine suggestions. Key features: translation memory that stores translated segments and offers matches (100 percent or fuzzy), terminology databases, alignment of existing translations, quality checks for numbers and spelling. Workflow: import the text, segment it, translate with matches, post-edit machine suggestions carefully, run quality checks and export. Ethics: confidentiality of client texts and human review, since machines make errors with context and culture.
sla_notes_illustrations: In OmegaT a sentence Le dossier est en cours de traitement is translated once as Faili inashughulikiwa; when the same segment appears later the tool proposes the stored translation automatically.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translation agencies and organisations use CAT tools to translate large documents quickly and keep terms consistent.
sla_exercise: What is a translation memory?::A database of previously translated segments that the tool offers for reuse.||Name one CAT tool.::OmegaT (or Trados or MemoQ).||Why must machine translation be post-edited?::Because it can make errors in meaning, context and style.

sla_method: Jeu de rôle/ dialogue ou simulation
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’interpréter correctement des dialogues et des discours complexes de divers contextes de communication formelle de manière simultanée ou consécutive.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels portant sur des sujets de contexte formel|Objets réels ou images d'équipment d'interprétation:|Écouteur|Micro|Micro-casque
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Interpreting is the oral transfer of a spoken message from one language into another. Learners practise simultaneous and consecutive modes in formal settings.
sla_notes_details: In consecutive interpreting the speaker pauses and the interpreter renders the message using notes; in simultaneous interpreting the interpreter speaks at almost the same time as the speaker, usually from a booth with headphones. Skills include active listening, memory, note-taking with symbols, paraphrasing, decalage (short delay), clear voice and neutrality. Preparation involves researching the topic and glossaries. Contexts are conferences, courts, diplomatic meetings and business negotiations. Learners practise with short dialogues and speeches and evaluate accuracy, completeness and fluency.
sla_notes_illustrations: A learner listens to a 30-second speech on health in French, notes key words with symbols, and then renders it in Swahili in front of the class, who assess accuracy and fluency.
sla_notes_daily_life: Interpreters are needed at conferences, courts, tourism and international meetings held in Tanzania.
sla_exercise: Differentiate consecutive from simultaneous interpreting.::In consecutive the interpreter speaks after the speaker pauses, in simultaneous the interpreter speaks almost at the same time as the speaker.||Name one skill an interpreter needs.::Active listening (or memory, note-taking, neutrality).||Where is simultaneous interpreting often used?::At conferences and international meetings.

sla_method: Recherche internet ou dans la bibliothèque

sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels portant sur de grands écrivains de la littérature francophone et leurs œuvres|Textes authentiques écrits des écrivains francophones africains
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Francophone literature is literature written in French in France and in other parts of the world, including Africa, the Caribbean and Canada. Learners get to know important authors and works.
sla_notes_details: Authors include Victor Hugo (Les Misérables), Molière (Le Malade imaginaire), Albert Camus (L'Étranger), Antoine de Saint-Exupéry (Le Petit Prince), Léopold Sédar Senghor (Chants d'ombre), Aimé Césaire (Cahier d'un retour au pays natal), Mariama Bâ (Une si longue lettre), Ferdinand Oyono (Une vie de boy), Camara Laye (L'Enfant noir), Cheikh Hamidou Kane (L'Aventure ambiguë) and Ahmadou Kourouma. Learners research the life, period, movement (romanticism, realism, négritude) and themes of each author and present them.
sla_notes_illustrations: Presentation on Mariama Bâ: born in Senegal in 1929; her novel Une si longue lettre (1979) deals with polygamy, women's status and friendship in the form of a letter.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing these authors helps learners to appreciate culture and to speak about literature in French-speaking communities.
sla_exercise: Who wrote Le Petit Prince?::Antoine de Saint-Exupéry.||Name one author of the négritude movement.::Léopold Sédar Senghor (or Aimé Césaire).||Which novel by Mariama Bâ is well known?::Une si longue lettre.

sla_name: Analysing literary works: stories and novels
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’analyser correctement et avec confiance des différents œuvres littéraires (récits, romans).
sla_teaching_aids: Œuvres littéraires proposés dans le programme de lecture et d’autres (récits|Romans)
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Literary analysis studies how a work is constructed and what it means. Learners analyse narratives and novels by Francophone writers.
sla_notes_details: Elements: summary of the plot, characters (protagonist, antagonist, secondary), setting (time and place), narrator and point of view (first person, third person omniscient), narrative structure (situation initiale, élément perturbateur, péripéties, dénouement, situation finale), themes, tone and style (figures of speech such as metaphor, comparison, personification) and the message. Learners write commentaries with an introduction, analysis supported by quotations and a conclusion, and discuss the social context of the work.
sla_notes_illustrations: In L'Enfant noir by Camara Laye the narrator is the author himself (first person); the theme is childhood in Guinea and the tension between tradition and modern education.
sla_notes_daily_life: Analytical skills help learners to think critically about stories, films and events in their own society.
sla_exercise: Name the stage of a story in which the problem appears.::L'élément perturbateur (the disturbing element).||What is a first person narrator?::A narrator who tells the story as I, taking part in it.||Give one figure of speech.::Metaphor (or comparison, personification).

main_competence_name: Apprécier et composer des œuvres littéraires
specific_competence_name: Composer des œuvres littéraires
learning_activity_name: Composer un récit et un roman
sla_name: Composing a short story and a novel
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de composer correctement un récit et un roman.
sla_teaching_aids: Récits|Romans
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners use their imagination and language skills to compose narratives in French, from a short story to the plan and opening chapters of a novel.
sla_notes_details: Steps: choose theme and genre, create characters and setting, plan the plot with the narrative schema, choose the narrator and tenses (passé simple or passé composé for events, imparfait for descriptions), write with dialogues and descriptions, use lively vocabulary and literary devices, then revise and edit. A novel needs chapters, a longer plot, subplots and character development; learners write a chapter plan and one or two chapters. The work is presented in class or published in a school magazine.
sla_notes_illustrations: Opening: Il était une fois, dans un petit village au pied du Kilimandjaro, une jeune fille nommée Neema qui rêvait de devenir médecin. Un matin, une lettre inattendue changea sa vie.
sla_notes_daily_life: Creative writing develops imagination and can lead to careers in writing, journalism and film.
sla_exercise: Which tense is used for descriptions in a narrative?::The imparfait.||Name the parts of the narrative schema.::Initial situation, disturbing element, events, resolution and final situation.||What is a chapter plan?::An outline of the events planned for each chapter of the novel.

sla_name: Phonetics and phonology rules in isolated words and connected speech
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’utiliser les règles de la phonétique et de la phonologie dans des mots isolés et dans l’enchaînement.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels de sujets variés|Documents authentiques écrits portant sur la phonétique et la phonologie
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The rules of phonetics and phonology explain how French sounds are produced and how they change in isolated words and in continuous speech.
sla_notes_details: In isolated words learners apply the correspondence between spelling and sounds: silent final consonants (petit, grand), the letter combinations ou [u], oi [wa], eau [o], ch [ʃ], gn [ɲ], the different values of s between vowels [z] and of c before e or i [s], and the mute e. Vowel oppositions such as u and ou, é and è, and nasal vowels are practised. In connected speech the rules of liaison, enchaînement, elision and the mute e (loi des trois consonnes) apply, together with assimilation, rhythm groups and intonation patterns. Learners transcribe words in the International Phonetic Alphabet and read phonetic transcriptions aloud.
sla_notes_illustrations: The phrase Il y a un petit oiseau is pronounced [il ja ɛ̃ pətitwazo], with liaison between petit and oiseau and enchaînement in il y a.
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct pronunciation helps in oral examinations, interviews and communication with French speakers.
sla_exercise: Give the pronunciation of eau.::[o].||Write the phonetic transcription of the word chat.::[ʃa].||What is the rule for the final consonant of petit before oiseau?::It is pronounced in liaison as [t]: petit oiseau [pətitwazo].

sla_name: Conversing in unfamiliar contexts
sla_method: Jeu de rôle/ dialogue ou simulation
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de converser dans des contextes non familiers (à la douane, au tribunal, à des conférences, à des réunions).
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels de situations de communication suivantes: à la douane|Au tribunal|À des conférences|À des réunions
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners use French in situations that are not part of their daily life, such as at customs, in court, at conferences and at meetings.
sla_notes_details: Each context has its own vocabulary and formulas. At customs: Avez-vous quelque chose à déclarer ? Voici mon passeport et mon visa. In court: le juge, l'avocat, le témoin, l'accusé, prêter serment, plaider, verdict. At conferences: présenter un exposé, poser une question, prendre la parole, l'ordre du jour. At meetings: ouvrir la séance, proposer, voter, adopter, procès-verbal. Learners use the formal register, polite forms and appropriate body language, and prepare through simulations and role plays, using glossaries of specialised terms.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role play at customs: Douanier - Bonjour, vos documents s'il vous plaît. Voyageur - Les voici. Douanier - Quel est le but de votre voyage ? Voyageur - Je participe à un séminaire à Kigali.
sla_notes_daily_life: These skills are needed by travellers, tour guides, lawyers, diplomats and workers at international conferences.
sla_exercise: Ask a traveller if he has anything to declare.::Avez-vous quelque chose à déclarer ?||What is a procès-verbal?::The official record (minutes) of a meeting.||Name two persons in a court.::The judge (le juge) and the lawyer (l'avocat).

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de rédiger correctement des récits longs avec le passé simple.
sla_teaching_aids: Récrits longs variés narrés en utilisant le temps passé
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: The passé simple is a literary past tense used in written narratives, tales, novels and history to present completed actions in the past.
sla_notes_details: Formation: for -er verbs the endings are -ai, -as, -a, -âmes, -âtes, -èrent (parler: je parlai, il parla, ils parlèrent); for -ir and -re verbs the endings are -is, -is, -it, -îmes, -îtes, -irent (finir: il finit); for irregular verbs the endings are -us or -ins (avoir: il eut; être: il fut; venir: il vint; faire: il fit; voir: il vit). It is used mostly in the third person with the imparfait for description and background: Il pleuvait quand le voyageur arriva. Long narratives need a plan, characters, chronological or flashback order, connectors of time and consistent tenses.
sla_notes_illustrations: Il fut un temps où le roi régnait sur tout le pays. Un jour, un étranger arriva au village, frappa à la porte et demanda un verre d'eau.
sla_notes_daily_life: The passé simple is found in classic and modern novels and tales, so mastering it is needed to read and write literary French.
sla_exercise: Give the passé simple of il parler.::Il parla.||Give the passé simple of il avoir and il être.::Il eut and il fut.||Which tense usually accompanies the passé simple for descriptions?::The imparfait.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de donner des discours sur des sujets variés en utilisant le français avec efficacité et autonomie.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents oraux/audio-visuels portant sur des discours de sujets variés|Documents authentiques écrits variés portant le vocabulaire et la grammaire cibles
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A speech is a prepared oral presentation to an audience. Learners deliver speeches on varied subjects with effectiveness and independence.
sla_notes_details: Structure: attractive opening that greets the audience and presents the topic (Mesdames et Messieurs, chers collègues...), body with two or three main points supported by examples and statistics, and a conclusion with a summary and a call to action (Je vous remercie de votre attention). Language features are rhetorical questions, repetition, contrasts, logical connectors and an appropriate register. Delivery includes voice projection, pace, pauses, eye contact and posture. Learners plan with notes, rehearse, and receive feedback using an assessment grid.
sla_notes_illustrations: A speech on youth employment might begin: Chers amis, que ferons-nous demain si nous n'apprenons pas à créer des emplois aujourd'hui ? and conclude: Ensemble, nous pouvons construire l'avenir. Merci.
sla_notes_daily_life: Speeches are given at school events, graduation ceremonies, community meetings and in political and business life.
sla_exercise: Name the three parts of a speech.::Introduction, body and conclusion.||Give a French phrase used to thank an audience.::Je vous remercie de votre attention.||What is a rhetorical question?::A question asked for effect and not to get an answer.

sla_name: Using synonyms and antonyms to compose texts
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’utiliser correctement des synonymes et des antonymes pour composer une variété de textes complexes.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques/ fabriqués oraux ou écrits portant sur des synonymes
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Synonyms are words with similar meanings and antonyms are words with opposite meanings. Using them enriches texts and avoids repetition.
sla_notes_details: Synonyms are rarely exactly identical and vary by register and nuance: grand, immense, vaste; beau, magnifique, splendide; dire, affirmer, déclarer, prétendre. Antonyms are opposites: grand and petit, joie and tristesse, accepter and refuser, and antonyms formed with prefixes such as heureux and malheureux, possible and impossible, légal and illégal. Learners use dictionaries and thesauri to choose the word that best fits the context, use them for cohesion (replace a repeated word) and for contrast in descriptive and argumentative texts.
sla_notes_illustrations: Instead of repeating beau three times: Le paysage est magnifique, la plage splendide et le village charmant. In an argument: La ville attire par ses opportunités mais repousse par ses inconvénients.
sla_notes_daily_life: A rich vocabulary makes reports, articles and letters more convincing and pleasant to read.
sla_exercise: Give a synonym of important.::Essentiel (or capital, majeur).||Give the antonym of légal.::Illégal.||Why should writers use synonyms?::To avoid repetition and to express ideas more precisely.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de composer avec autonomie des textes portant sur des domaines spécifiques (journalisme, droit, médicine) en utilisant le vocabulaire et la grammaire avancée.
sla_teaching_aids: Textes complexes authentiques des domaines spécifiques: journalisme|Droit|Et médicine
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Specialised fields have their own vocabulary, structures and text types. Learners write texts for journalism, law and medicine using advanced vocabulary and grammar.
sla_notes_details: Journalism: news reports answer who, what, where, when, why and how (5W and H), with headline, lead paragraph and body in the inverted pyramid; reported speech and the present tense of news headlines. Law: legal terms such as loi, article, tribunal, plainte, contrat, droit, obligation, and formal structures with the future and subjunctive (Le locataire est tenu de payer). Medicine: terms such as symptôme, diagnostic, ordonnance, traitement, maladie, and texts such as patient information, prescriptions and health campaign messages. Accuracy, clarity and objectivity are required.
sla_notes_illustrations: News headline and lead: Kilimandjaro : un incendie ravage la forêt. Un incendie s'est déclaré lundi sur les pentes de la montagne et a détruit plus de 300 hectares, selon les autorités.
sla_notes_daily_life: Skills are useful for future journalists, lawyers, doctors, nurses and translators of specialised documents.
sla_exercise: What do the 5W and H stand for in a news report?::Who, what, where, when, why and how.||Give one legal term in French.::Le tribunal (or la loi, le contrat, la plainte).||Translate: prescription (medicine).::Ordonnance.

specific_competence_name: Développer la compréhension des conversations en français
learning_activity_name: Écouter et répondre oralement à des informations en utilisant les caractéristiques inhérentes de la langue parlée
sla_name: Responding to spoken information using features of spoken language
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’écouter et de répondre oralement à des informations en utilisant correctement les caractéristiques inhérentes de la langue parlée.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques oraux/audio-visuels portant des caractéristiques inhérentes visées de la langue parlée
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Spoken language has features that written language does not: rhythm, intonation, hesitations, repetitions, interruptions and informal expressions. Learners respond orally by understanding these features.
sla_notes_details: Features include rising and falling intonation showing questions, surprise or doubt; stress for emphasis (C'est vraiment intéressant); fillers (euh, bon, ben, alors, tu vois); dropping of ne in negation (je sais pas); contractions (t'as, j'suis, y a); dislocation (Ton frère, je le connais); repetition and self-correction; and speed. Listening activities use interviews, radio conversations and videos. Learners identify these features, understand what the speaker means and reply orally with appropriate turns and reactions such as Ah bon ? C'est vrai ? Tout à fait.
sla_notes_illustrations: In a recorded conversation: Ben, j'sais pas... euh... je crois que c'est demain. The learner replies: Ah, tu n'es pas sûr ? Je vais vérifier alors.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding real spoken French is essential for communicating with French speakers in conversation, on the telephone and in media.
sla_exercise: Give one feature of spoken French.::Dropping of ne in negation (or use of fillers and contractions).||What does euh show in speech?::Hesitation while the speaker thinks.||Which reaction expresses surprise?::Ah bon ? (or C'est vrai ?).

sla_name: Taking part in interviews
sla_method: Jeu de rôle/ dialogue ou simulation
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de prendre part à des entretiens avec confiance et autonomie.
sla_teaching_aids: Document authentiques oraux/audio-visuels/ écrits portant sur des entrentiens

sla_notes_intro: An interview is a structured conversation in which an interviewer asks questions and an interviewee answers. Learners take both roles with confidence.
sla_notes_details: Types are job interviews, media interviews and survey interviews. Preparation includes researching the organisation or person, preparing questions and possible answers, and a curriculum vitae. Questions: Parlez-moi de vous, Pourquoi voulez-vous ce poste ? Quels sont vos points forts ? Answers are clear, honest and organised, using formal language and the conditional for politeness (Je souhaiterais...). Interviewers use open questions and follow-up questions. Non-verbal behaviour includes greeting, posture, eye contact and thanking at the end.
sla_notes_illustrations: Interviewer - Pourquoi avez-vous choisi le tourisme ? Candidate - J'aime rencontrer des gens de différentes cultures et je parle plusieurs langues, ce qui me permettrait d'accueillir les visiteurs francophones.
sla_notes_daily_life: Interviews are a part of job selection, scholarship applications and radio and television programmes.
sla_exercise: Ask a candidate to introduce himself in French.::Parlez-moi de vous.||Name one type of interview.::Job interview (or media interview or survey).||Why is the conditional used in polite answers?::It softens requests and shows politeness, for example Je souhaiterais...

sla_notes_intro: Cross-cutting issues such as the environment, gender, HIV and AIDS, corruption, technology, human rights and entrepreneurship concern all subjects. Learners discuss them in French using advanced vocabulary and complex sentences.
sla_notes_details: Vocabulary for the environment: le réchauffement climatique, la déforestation, les énergies renouvelables, la biodiversité. Gender and rights: l'égalité, la discrimination, l'autonomisation. Technology: l'intelligence artificielle, la cybersécurité, les réseaux sociaux. Complex structures include relative clauses (ce qui, ce que, dont), concession (même si, bien que), condition (à condition que + subjunctive), purpose (afin que, pour que + subjunctive), and cause and consequence (en raison de, grâce à, par conséquent). Learners give opinions, present arguments and propose solutions.
sla_notes_illustrations: Il est essentiel que les gouvernements développent les énergies renouvelables afin que les générations futures puissent vivre dans un environnement sain.
sla_notes_daily_life: These topics are discussed in national and international forums, and in the media where French is used.
sla_exercise: Translate: climate change.::Le changement climatique (or le réchauffement climatique).||What mood follows afin que?::The subjunctive.||Give a French expression of consequence.::Par conséquent (or donc, c'est pourquoi).

sla_name: Writing academic texts with references: dissertations
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de rédiger correctement des textes académiques/ dissertations avec des références.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques écrits sur des essais académiques
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A dissertation is an academic essay that develops a reasoned argument on a question, supported by references. Learners write dissertations following French academic conventions.
sla_notes_details: Structure: introduction (accroche, présentation du sujet, problématique, annonce du plan), development in two or three parts with sub-parts (thèse, antithèse, synthèse or a thematic plan), each paragraph with an idea, an argument and an example, and a conclusion (réponse à la problématique et ouverture). Sources are cited with quotations in inverted commas, footnotes or in-text references (author, year) and a bibliography listing author, title, publisher and year. Plagiarism is avoided by paraphrasing and citing. Style is formal, impersonal and precise, with connectors between parts.
sla_notes_illustrations: Bibliography entry: Senghor, L. S. (1945). Chants d'ombre. Paris : Éditions du Seuil. In text: Comme l'affirme Senghor (1945), la culture est le fondement du développement.
sla_notes_daily_life: Dissertation skills are needed at university and in research reports and professional writing.
sla_exercise: What is the problématique of a dissertation?::The central question the essay tries to answer.||Name the three parts of a dialectic plan.::Thesis, antithesis and synthesis.||Why must sources be cited?::To acknowledge other authors and avoid plagiarism.

sla_notes_intro: Learners apply computer assisted translation tools to translate different types of complex texts such as legal, scientific, journalistic and technical documents.
sla_notes_details: Steps: analyse the text type and terminology; create a project in the CAT tool; import glossaries and translation memories; translate segment by segment; use concordance search to see how terms were translated before; post-edit machine translation suggestions; run spelling, terminology and number checks; and export in the original format. Learners compare their output with machine translation and discuss quality, style and fidelity. Specialised fields require reliable terminology sources such as FranceTerme and IATE.
sla_notes_illustrations: A legal notice in French is loaded in OmegaT; the glossary provides bailleur - mwenye nyumba and locataire - mpangaji; the tool proposes these terms in each segment, ensuring consistency.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translation bureaux use these tools to deliver large projects quickly and with consistent terminology.
sla_exercise: What is a glossary in translation?::A list of terms and their agreed translations.||What is concordance search?::A function that finds how a word or phrase was translated before in the memory.||Give one quality check done by a CAT tool.::Checking numbers, spelling or terminology consistency.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de créer des sous- titres pour les médias audio-visuels authentiques.
sla_teaching_aids: Logiciels|Documents audio-visuels avec sous-titres
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Subtitling means adding translated or transcribed text on screen in synchrony with the speech of a video or film. Learners create subtitles for audiovisual material.
sla_notes_details: Guidelines: a subtitle has at most two lines of about 35 to 42 characters, is displayed for one to six seconds according to reading speed (about 15 to 17 characters per second), and is synchronised with speech. Text is condensed without losing meaning, punctuation is simple, and line breaks follow phrases. Tools are Aegisub, Subtitle Edit and Amara; the SRT file format contains a number, the time code (00:00:05,000 --> 00:00:08,200) and the text. Learners transcribe, translate, time, review and export the subtitles, checking that they match the images and the culture.
sla_notes_illustrations: SRT block: 1, 00:00:05,000 --> 00:00:08,000, Bonjour à tous et bienvenue à Dar es Salaam. The Swahili subtitle is Habari zenu nyote na karibuni Dar es Salaam.
sla_notes_daily_life: Subtitling is used in films, television, online videos and educational material to reach people who speak other languages or have hearing difficulties.
sla_exercise: What is the maximum number of lines usually used in a subtitle?::Two lines.||Name one subtitling tool.::Aegisub (or Subtitle Edit or Amara).||What information does a time code give?::The time at which a subtitle appears and disappears.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’éditer et de relire correctement des textes complexes.
sla_teaching_aids: Documents authentiques écrits|Dictionnaires
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Editing improves the content, structure and style of a text, and proofreading corrects the remaining errors of spelling, grammar and punctuation before publication.
sla_notes_details: Editing checks the clarity of ideas, logical order, paragraphing, repetition, consistency of tenses and register, and the fit with the audience and purpose. Proofreading checks orthography and accents (é, è, ê), agreement of gender, number and past participles, verb conjugation, homophones (a and à, ou and où, ces and ses, on and ont), punctuation and typography (space before ; : ? !). Tools include correctors such as Antidote and Word, but a human reading is required. Standard proofreading marks are used, and versions are compared.
sla_notes_illustrations: Original: Les enfant sont aller a l'école. Corrected: Les enfants sont allés à l'école (plural marks, participle agreement and the preposition à).
sla_notes_daily_life: Editors and proofreaders work in publishing houses, newspapers and translation agencies to make sure published texts are correct.
sla_exercise: Correct the sentence: Elle est parti hier.::Elle est partie hier.||What is the difference between editing and proofreading?::Editing improves content and style, while proofreading corrects spelling, grammar and punctuation.||Choose the correct word: Il (a/à) un livre.::a.

sla_teaching_aids: Objets réels/ images d'équipement d’interprétation|Logiciels de voix hors champ et doublage
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Audiovisual interpreting adapts spoken content of videos into another language orally. Two main techniques are voice-over and dubbing.
sla_notes_details: In voice-over the original sound remains audible at a low volume while the interpreter speaks over it; it is used in documentaries and news. In dubbing the original voices are replaced by voices in the target language, synchronised with lip movements, a process that requires script adaptation, casting and recording. Learners analyse the video, prepare a script or interpret live, respect timing, tone and emotions, use a clear voice and avoid excessive rhythm changes. Tools include audio editing software such as Audacity and video editors. The quality is evaluated for accuracy, synchronisation and naturalness.
sla_notes_illustrations: A learner watches a two-minute French documentary about elephants and records a Swahili voice-over that begins a few seconds after the original speaker, with the French sound lowered.
sla_notes_daily_life: Voice-over and dubbing are used by television stations and film companies to broadcast foreign programmes in local languages.
sla_exercise: What is voice-over?::A technique where the translation is spoken over the original audio, which stays faintly audible.||What is dubbing?::Replacing the original voices in a film with voices in another language.||Name one audio editing tool.::Audacity.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’analyser correctement des poèmes et pièces de théâtre.
sla_teaching_aids: Textes littéraires stipulilés dans le programme de lecture (poèmes et théâtre)
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D'ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ve À VIe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Poetry and theatre are two literary genres with their own forms. Learners analyse poems and plays by Francophone authors.
sla_notes_details: Poetry: verse and stanza, rhyme schemes (rimes plates, croisées, embrassées), metre (alexandrin with twelve syllables, octosyllabe), sounds (alliteration, assonance), figures (métaphore, comparaison, personification, anaphore) and themes such as love, nature, nostalgia and négritude. Theatre: acts and scenes, stage directions (didascalies), dialogue, monologue and aside, characters, dramatic conflict, unity of time, place and action in classical theatre, genres (tragédie, comédie, drame). Learners read poems by Baudelaire, Senghor, David Diop and Rimbaud and plays by Molière, Corneille and Bernard Dadié, and write commentaries with quotations.
sla_notes_illustrations: In Senghor's poem Femme noire, the repetition of Femme nue, femme noire is an anaphore that praises African beauty and expresses love for the homeland.
sla_notes_daily_life: Studying poetry and theatre improves appreciation of art, sensitivity to language and public expression.
sla_exercise: What is an alexandrin?::A line of verse of twelve syllables.||What are didascalies?::Stage directions in a play.||Name one figure of speech and give its meaning.::Metaphor: an implicit comparison without a comparison word.

sla_notes_intro: Learners create their own poem and a short play in French, applying their knowledge of form and language.
sla_notes_details: Poem: choose a theme and feeling, decide the form (free verse or rhymed), select images and figures of speech, arrange the stanzas, care about rhythm and sound, and revise. Play: choose the theme and characters, plan the scenes, write dialogues with stage directions, create conflict and resolution, and consider setting, props and costumes. Language points include the register appropriate to each character, present tense for dialogues and imperative in stage directions. Works are performed or read aloud, published in a school anthology and assessed with a criteria grid.
sla_notes_illustrations: Poem opening: Ô mon Kilimandjaro, roi de neige et de soleil, / Tu veilles sur mes rêves comme un père sur son sommeil. Play: Scène 1 - Une cour d'école. NEEMA (entrant en courant) : Je suis en retard !
sla_notes_daily_life: Creative expression in poems and plays is used in festivals, school drama clubs and cultural events.
sla_exercise: What are didascalies used for when writing a play?::To describe actions, settings and tone for the actors.||Name one way to give rhythm to a poem.::Using regular verses and rhyme (or repetition).||Complete the rhyme: soleil, ...::sommeil (or réveil).
